questionBoundQualifications.sourceClaim: Page 990 categorically says a robot cannot plan, navigate or grasp using raw pixels directly; page 1007 introduces learned detection.
questionBoundQualifications.qualification: The lecture motivates extracting informative representations. It does not establish that explicit hand-engineered feature extraction is a universal prerequisite for every pixel-input model.

questionBoundQualifications.sourceClaim: Caption calls h=15 a window size of 15, while preceding slide shows μ−kσ; official API defines half-width and mean-minus-C.
questionBoundQualifications.qualification: With h=15, 2h+1=31. The documented default API uses a neighborhood mean minus C, so the caption and preceding generic formula must not be treated as literal API semantics.

questionBoundQualifications.sourceClaim: The displayed matrix expression retains L(λ) but directly equates its result to color-matching functions without stating stimulus normalization.
questionBoundQualifications.qualification: The printed final equality suppresses the stimulus normalization. Unit-stimulus matching functions must be distinguished from coefficients for an arbitrarily scaled stimulus.

questionBoundQualifications.sourceClaim: Source attributes all three primary choices to mercury vapor emission lines; this historical attribution is not established here and is excluded from the tested claim.
questionBoundQualifications.qualification: The page lists the three wavelength values and depicts illuminant, reflecting object and eye. The separate attribution of all three wavelengths to mercury lines is not used as a factual premise.

questionBoundQualifications.sourceClaim: The color-constancy motivation can be read as full illumination invariance; the tested workflow only omits the lightness coordinate.
questionBoundQualifications.qualification: L* represents lightness and a*,b* the opponent chromatic coordinates. Removing L* changes the metric used for clustering but does not make k-means parameter-free or universally illumination-invariant.

questionBoundQualifications.sourceClaim: Source prose describes m as object count with labels 0,…,m, but the API returns the number of all labels N with range 0,…,N−1.
questionBoundQualifications.qualification: The returned N includes the background. Four foreground objects occupy labels 1–4, while N=5.

questionBoundQualifications.sourceClaim: The source uses atan(v_y/v_x) without quadrant, zero-denominator or equal-eigenvalue qualifications.
questionBoundQualifications.qualification: A robust interpretation uses atan2(v_y,v_x), treats opposite vectors as the same axis and recognizes isotropic degeneracy.

questionBoundQualifications.sourceClaim: The slide attributes invariance to seven scalars from central moments without explicitly stating the scale normalization.
questionBoundQualifications.qualification: Hu invariants use normalized central moments, not merely arbitrary unnormalized moments. Sampling and numerical precision affect practical invariance.

questionBoundQualifications.sourceClaim: The displayed J3 array references u11 and u02 without defining them in the excerpt.
questionBoundQualifications.qualification: The excerpt needs, for example, u11=blobs[3].moments.mu11 and u02=blobs[3].moments.mu02. Those are added context, not lines already present in the slide.

questionBoundQualifications.sourceClaim: The area-as-pixel-count discussion and fractional blob contour area use different conventions without an explicit distinction.
questionBoundQualifications.qualification: The blob API derives shape measurements from contours. Its continuous polygon area can have half-unit values, unlike a direct integer pixel sum.

questionBoundQualifications.sourceClaim: The slide suggests radius signatures distinguish shapes regardless of orientation without stating phase alignment.
questionBoundQualifications.qualification: Centroid-to-boundary distances can support rotation-robust matching, but their ordering must be aligned or handled invariantly.

questionBoundQualifications.sourceClaim: The polar call uses blobs[0], but the associated caption says radius and theta of blob 3.
questionBoundQualifications.qualification: The source code/caption mismatch must be preserved rather than silently replacing the index.

questionBoundQualifications.sourceClaim: The slide describes Faster R-CNN in pixel-classification/instance-segmentation terms while showing detector boxes.
questionBoundQualifications.qualification: Standard Faster R-CNN detection must not be conflated with mask prediction. The inspected street figure supports boxes and labels, not complete pixel masks.

questionBoundQualifications.sourceClaim: The theory slide uses Euclidean gradient magnitude, while the shown Canny call leaves its default L1 magnitude option unchanged.
questionBoundQualifications.qualification: The mathematical presentation and the displayed API defaults are not identical. State the norm explicitly when reproducing numerical behavior.

questionBoundQualifications.sourceClaim: The source calls I_u and I_v derivatives of a Gaussian; in the matrix they must be image gradients obtained using suitable derivative filters.
questionBoundQualifications.qualification: Image derivatives may be computed by derivative-of-Gaussian filtering, but the structure matrix is built from the resulting image-gradient products.

questionBoundQualifications.sourceClaim: The summary jointly describes Harris and SIFT as robust to scale changes without distinguishing fixed-scale Harris.
questionBoundQualifications.qualification: Harris corners at a fixed scale can disappear or change character when the image scale changes. SIFT incorporates characteristic-scale selection.

questionBoundQualifications.sourceClaim: The slide calls DoG an approximation to LoG without explicitly stating the scale-normalized proportional relationship.
questionBoundQualifications.qualification: Subtracting nearby Gaussian scale levels approximates a proportional scale-normalized LoG response, which motivates efficient scale-space extrema detection.

questionBoundQualifications.sourceClaim: The slide comment suggests top 50% of keypoints, but percentstrength uses a fraction of maximum response, not a count percentile.
questionBoundQualifications.qualification: The strength threshold is 5; A,B,C pass it, then B is removed for scale 4. This is not selecting half of the feature count.

questionBoundQualifications.sourceClaim: The figure shows an ellipse on each blob while the excerpt explicitly constructs and plots only J3 at the blob3 centroid.
questionBoundQualifications.qualification: The actual slide figure contains multiple ellipses, but the displayed excerpt explicitly issues only one ellipse call. Additional plotting context would be needed to reproduce all four.

additionalPreservedQualifications.handling: Questions explicitly specify the displayed convention.

additionalPreservedQualifications.handling: Record exact package result; source-value questions do not assert identical cross-version output.

additionalPreservedQualifications.handling: They describe the same unoriented axes; checked moduloπ, not called a source defect.

additionalPreservedQualifications.handling: Execution confirms strict threshold, so the comment is consistent and not marked conflicting.

additionalPreservedQualifications.handling: Numeric source primary list is tested separately; historical attribution remains unresolved.

Contour measurements, radius profiles and polar cross-correlation.
